yarn-troppo.meaning: All technical content survives, commands and links intact: "generate a trait object vtable with a null pointer", "rustup default beta", "locally and in your CI". Additions react to the text: "Not ideal.", "you'd be lucky if that's all", "Don't be shy.", "and that's the honest truth". The thanks link now reads "Cheers, legends!".
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "easy as", "No wukkas", "the guts of it", "par for the course", "keen", "pitched in". "the excuse for arbitrary effects" is a fair take on "justification".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural lines ("getting Rust 1.98.1 is easy as. Just run:", "No wukkas"), but several stock openers bolted on: "G'day, Rustaceans.", "For anyone who's been living under a rock", "Cheers, legends!"
yarn-troppo.register: Full level 4: friendly-mate voice all the way through. No swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: The release note's friendly tone is pushed toward banter; "For anyone who's been living under a rock" adds a mild jab the original lacks.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads well; the added beats break up the technical paragraph: "sitting right where a function pointer ought to be. Not ideal. That leads to undefined behaviour".
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied: "G'day", "every man and his dog", "easy as", "No wukkas", "Righto", "par for the course", "Don't be shy", "legends".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the 1.98.1 notes, structure and links intact.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Faithful throughout, commands and links intact: "under some conditions, rustc would wrongly generate a trait object vtable", "it can also be the excuse for arbitrary effects".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "every man and his dog" for "everyone", "par for the course" for "typical", "keen", "pitched in", "the lot of you".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, idiom used as locals do: "If you're keen to give us a hand by testing future releases".
yarn-dinkum.register: Light for level 4: much of the text is close to the original, slang limited to a handful of phrases ("every man and his dog", "par for the course", "keen", "Heaps").
yarn-dinkum.tone: The original's friendly, technical tone is intact.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "Heaps of people pitched in to make Rust 1.98.1."

unharnessed.meaning: Technical content intact. "build software that's reliable and runs like a bloody dream" stretches "efficient"; "any old weird effects at all" for "arbitrary effects" is right. "the mongrel" is an aside.
unharnessed.sense: Terms mostly fit: "stuff up", "sorts out", "code it spits out", "fair game" (UB licenses anything), "trip over", "lend us a hand". "runs like a bloody dream" reads as speed rather than efficiency, a slight strain.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural ("rustc would go and stuff up a trait object vtable", "the lot of youse"), but "got an older version of Rust in through rustup" is clumsy.
unharnessed.register: Full level 4 with dad-level swearing in bounds: "runs like a bloody dream", "the mongrel". Within vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.tone: Still a release note, but "(as you'd expect with UB, the mongrel)" and "a bloody dream" add a larrikin edge to a neutral announcement.
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth; one awkward join: "If you've already got an older version of Rust in through rustup".
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "pushed out", "leg-up", "grabbing", "sorts out", "stuff up", "spits out", "fair game", "mongrel", "trip over", "youse".

engine.meaning: The original verbatim apart from two swaps; nothing lost.
engine.sense: "empowering every man and his dog" keeps the sense of "everyone".
engine.authenticity: One stock phrase dropped into corporate prose: "Rust is a programming language that is empowering every man and his dog".
engine.register: Untranslated apart from "every man and his dog" and "behaviour": far under level 4.
engine.flow: Reads as the original; "empowering every man and his dog" is a jarring mix.
engine.variety: One slang phrase in the whole text.
engine.essence: What it says is the original.

dinkum-3.meaning: Faithful throughout, commands and links intact: "rustc would get it wrong and generate a trait object vtable with a null pointer", "it can be grounds for arbitrary effects too". "Good news:" is a light frame.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "every man and his dog", "No worries", "par for the course", "keen", "have a go at", "pitched in". "grounds for" renders "justification" well.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural, nothing forced: "Haven't got it yet? No worries, you can get rustup from the right page on our website."
dinkum-3.register: Level 4 in voice and kept within a technical note's bounds; slang moderate ("No worries", "keen", "Heaps"). No swearing, within the dial. A touch light.
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth: "Back in Rust 1.98.0, in some cases, rustc would get it wrong and generate a trait object vtable".
